questions.question: Which of the following options is correct for Coulomb's law?

options.text: Valid for both point and distributed charges
Valid for neither point charge nor distributed charge

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Valid for only point charge.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Coulomb's law:-**

 
 
• It is a fundamental law of electrostatics that describes the interaction between electric charges.
 
• It states that the force between two point charges is directly proportional to the product of their charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them. 
 
• While Coulomb's law is only valid for point charges, the principle can be extended to calculate the force between distributed charges by treating them as a collection of point charges.
 
• Coulomb's law is a fundamental principle that is used extensively in electrostatics, including in the design of electrical circuits and devices.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A point charge is a theoretical concept used to describe a charge that is concentrated at a single point in space.
 
• Distributed charges are charges that are spread out over a surface or volume.

questions.question: Which ecologist showed in a long-term experiment on outdoor plots that biodiversity is of central importance to the productivity, stability, resistance to the invasion of ecosystems and fertility of their soils?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**David Tilman.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **David Tilman:-**

 
 
• He showed in his long-term experiment on outdoor plots that biodiversity is essential to the productivity, stability, resistance to invasion of ecosystems, and fertility of their soils.
 
• His experiment involved growing different combinations of plant species and measuring the resulting productivity and stability of the ecosystem.
 
• The results showed that ecosystems with higher biodiversity were more productive and stable, and had greater resistance to invasion by non-native species.
 
• This experiment supports the idea that preserving biodiversity is crucial for maintaining healthy and functioning ecosystems. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Karl Mobius:-**

 
 
• He was a German zoologist who studied marine ecosystems, but did not conduct research on the importance of biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Herbert Spencer:-**
 
 
• He was a 19th-century philosopher and sociologist who did not conduct any research on ecology or biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Edward Osborne Wilson:-**
 
 
• He is a renowned biologist who has done extensive research on biodiversity.

questions.question:
Match the items is List I with those in List II.

 
 

 
 **Measure of National Income**
 
 **Formula**
 
 

 i.
 GNP
 a.
 GNP - Depreciation
 
 

 ii.
 NNP
 b.
 C + I + G + Net exports
 
 

 iii.
 GDP
 c.
 GDP - Depreciation
 
 

 iv.
 NDP
 d.
 GDP + Net factor income from abroad

options.text: i - b, ii - d, iii - a, iv - c
i - a, ii - c, iii - d, iv - b
i - d, ii - a, iii - b, iv - c
i - c, ii - b, iii - d, iv - a

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** i - d, ii - a, iii - b, iv - c.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **GNP:-**

 
 
• Gross National Product is the total value of goods and services produced by a country's residents, including those produced abroad, and can be calculated as C (consumption) + I (investment) + G (government spending) + net exports (exports - imports).
 
 
 
• **NNP:-**
 
 
• (Net National Product) is the GNP minus depreciation, which is the decrease in value of capital goods over time due to wear and tear.
 
 
 
• **GDP:-**
 
 
• (Gross Domestic Product) is the total value of goods and services produced within a country's borders, and can be calculated as C + I + G + net exports.
 
 
 
• **NDP:-**
 
 
• (Net Domestic Product) is the GDP minus depreciation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National income measures:-**

 
 
• These are important indicators of a country's economic performance and are used for policy-making and analysis.
 
• Another measure of national income is GNI (Gross National Income), which is similar to GNP but includes net income from abroad and excludes net taxes and subsidies.
 
• Per capita measures of national income, such as GDP per capita or GNP per capita, can provide insights into the standard of living of a country's population.
 
• National income measures have limitations and do not capture important aspects of economic activity, such as non-market activities, informal sector, and environmental degradation.

questions.question: Ebony, mahogany, and rosewood trees are part of which type of forest?

__
 
• ** Tropical evergreen forests:-**

 
 
• These are also known as rainforests, which are characterized by high rainfall and year-round warm temperatures.
 
• Ebony, mahogany, and rosewood trees are part of the Tropical evergreen forest.
 
• These forests are home to a diverse range of flora and fauna and are considered one of the most biologically diverse ecosystems on the planet.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Temperate forests:-**

 
 
• These are found in regions with moderate temperatures and distinct seasons, such as the northeastern United States, Europe, and parts of Asia.
 
• Trees commonly found in temperate forests include oak, maple, and birch.
 
 
 
• **Tropical deciduous forests:-**
 
 
• These are found in regions with seasonal rainfall, such as India and Africa.
 
• Trees commonly found in tropical deciduous forests include sal, teak, and eucalyptus.
 
 
 
• **Alpine vegetation:-**
 
 
• These refers to the plants that grow at high altitudes, typically above the tree line.
 
• These plants are adapted to the harsh conditions of high altitude environments, such as cold temperatures and low oxygen levels.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that laws that are inconsistent with or in derogation of any of the fundamental rights shall be void?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 13**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 13 of the Indian Constitution:-**

 
 
• **It mentions that laws that are inconsistent with or in derogation of any of the fundamental rights shall be void.**
 
• This means that any law that goes against the fundamental rights guaranteed by the Constitution will be deemed invalid and unenforceable.
 
• Fundamental rights are an important aspect of the Indian Constitution and are enshrined in Part III of the Constitution.
 
• These rights include the right to equality, right to freedom, right against exploitation, right to freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and the right to constitutional remedies.
 
• The Constitution also provides for the protection of these fundamental rights through the mechanism of the judiciary, which can strike down any law that violates these rights. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 14 of the Constitution:-**

 
 
• It guarantees the right to equality before the law and equal protection of the law to all citizens.
 
 
 
• **Article 15:-**
 
 
• It prohibits discrimination on the grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.
 
 
 
• **Article 16:-**
 
 
• It guarantees equality of opportunity in matters of public employment and prohibits discrimination on the grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, residence or any of them.

questions.question: Who among the following rulers invaded Malaya to liberate their trade with China?

• **Chola**:-

 
 
• **The ruler who invaded Malaya to liberate their trade with China was the Chola dynasty.**
 
• The Cholas were a powerful dynasty that ruled over a large part of South India from the 9th to the 13th century.
 
• The Cholas were known for their naval power and trade with Southeast Asia, particularly with China.
 
• The Cholas invaded Malaya (modern-day Malaysia) in the 11th century to establish a trade relationship with China, which was being blocked by the Srivijaya empire that controlled the Strait of Malacca.

• **Pallava dynasty:-**

 
 
• The Pallava dynasty ruled over parts of South India from the 3rd to the 9th century and were known for their patronage of art and architecture, particularly the rock-cut temples at Mamallapuram.
 
 
 
• **Chalukya dynasty:-**
 
 
• The Chalukya dynasty ruled over parts of South and Central India from the 6th to the 12th century and were known for their architectural achievements, particularly the temples at Aihole and Pattadakal.
 
 
 
• **Rashtrakuta dynasty:-**
 
 
• The Rashtrakuta dynasty ruled over parts of Central and Southern India from the 8th to the 10th century and were known for their patronage of art and literature, particularly the Jain literature of the Kannada language.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the factors that has contributed towards localisation of the cotton textile industry in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** dry Climate.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points____​__**

 
• **Cotton textile industry:-**

 
 
• **The cotton textile industry is one of the oldest and largest industries in India, with a rich history dating back to ancient times.**
 
• India is the second-largest producer of cotton in the world, after China.
 
• The textile industry in India is concentrated in several regions, including Gujarat, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• **Other factors that have contributed to the growth of the cotton textile industry in India include government policies, technological advancements, and the availability of finance and infrastructure.**
 
• **Dry climate is not a factor that has contributed towards localisation of the cotton textile industry in India. In fact, a moderate climate with adequate rainfall is necessary for the growth of cotton.**
 
• Accessible port facilities have been a key factor in the development of the cotton textile industry in India, as they facilitate the export of finished goods and the import of raw materials.
 
• Availability of labour is also an important factor, as India has a large workforce that is skilled in textile production.
 
• Availability of raw cotton is another crucial factor, as India is one of the largest producers of cotton in the world.
